With the implication, the existential is satisfied by any handler who is not equipped (the if-part is false, so the implication is vacuously true). Counterexample: one fragile pallet p, one handler h who is not equipped and lifts nothing. The requirement is violated (no equipped handler lifts p), yet the formal statement is true, since equipped(h) → lifts(h, p) holds vacuously. This is exactly the case the requirement warns against ("a handler that is not equipped does not count").

The formal statement is therefore strictly weaker than the requirement (it only fails when handlers exist, all are equipped, and none lifts the pallet — or when no handlers exist).
